| # | Part | Topic |
|--:|---|---|
| 1 | [Intro]{.part .part-gen} | Course overview, logistics, study materials and exam; the questions the course answers |
| 2 | [Intro]{.part .part-gen} | Cyber-physical systems; the power system as the reference example |
| 3 | [Intro]{.part .part-gen} | Known cyber-physical attacks; risk management: process, quantitative approach, standards and regulations |
| 4 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | Modelling of the plant: state space models, with a mechanical example |
| 5 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | More examples; the notion of state, simulation models, discretization, change of coordinates |
| 6 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | The networked cyber-physical system: plant, controller, detector, networks, attacker; the attack space |
| 7 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | First attack models: eavesdropping, bias injection, denial of service, replay |
| 8 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | Solution of the linear state space model, part 1 |
| 9 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | Solution of the linear state space model, part 2: natural modes |
| 10 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | Stability of equilibria, continuous and discrete time; linearized models |
| 11 | [Model]{.part .part-model} | Monitors and their consistency; fundamental limitations of detection; undetectable and unidentifiable attacks |
| 12 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | False data injection against state estimation: linearized power flow, weighted least squares |
| 13 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Solution of the estimation problem, bad data detection, attack formulation, undetectability and impact |
| 14 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Security indices, attacks in a protected scenario, optimal protection |
| 15 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Exercise and simulations (Matlab); the security index as a mixed-integer program (Julia) |
| 16 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Generalizations: topology attacks, load redistribution attacks, multi-level attacks |
| 17 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Switching attacks; introduction to load altering attacks |
| 18 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Load altering attacks: model of the grid under attack, minimum destabilizing gain |
| 19 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Load altering attacks: vulnerability analysis and optimal protection |
| 20 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Zero dynamics attacks: scenario, goals, model, impact on state and output |
| 21 | [Attacks]{.part .part-att} | Zero dynamics attacks, conclusion; covert attacks |
| 22 | [Defence]{.part .part-def} | Detection with side initial state information; detectors and observers; watermarking |
| 23 | [Defence]{.part .part-def} | Secure control allocation; encrypted control |
| 24 | [Defence]{.part .part-def} [Wrap-up]{.part .part-gen} | Resilient control; course recap, exam and projects |
